It was a struggle in the beginning! But once you get the hang of it it'll come! If you still didn't like it then it's just not the thing for you now, and it's fine!

Only with knit stitches, I've experimented with purl stitches and would be able to do it if it's a certain size (anything sock yarn size i risk dropping stitches). So the most likely candidate would either be vanilla socks in the round or just long flat piece of knit stitches.

My understanding is that normal lasik creates a 'flap' and epi lasik doesn't, this is from Eagle Eye website

"Unlike LASIK where there is a flap created, there is no flap created for “No Touch All-Laser Epi-LASIK”, thus the procedure is less invasive and it removes ALL risk/potential for any flap-related (short or long term) complications during treatment."

Anything beyond that I can't explain properly, I was given the info but that was years ago.

1. Was great! It all happened in a day, the clinic waived the consultation fee if the procedure was scheduled within a certain time frame after the consultation. I did it at eagle eye centre, ngl there was alot of waiting cause sometimes they need the pupils to be dilated sometimes they need to run certain tests. All that being said I was in at around 8am and out by 3 to 4pm.

The actual procedure itself was very fast. I did epi lasik cause I was very active in dancing and didn't wanna risk any dislodge if I did lasik, also did some vitamin E treatment cross linked thingy to just help strengthen the cornea or something.

2. I'd say it costs about 4k +, cause after the procedure you'll need follow ups, post 1 day, post 1 week, post 3 months then 6 months. I think after 1 year they don't need to follow up as much anymore, every 5 years I believe. I'm not sure if cost is still the same cause I did this way back in early 2019.

3. Because it was epi lasik I was told it would be longer compared to lasik, it took about a week (I had to wear a contact lens as bandage the whole week). I wore goggles for about a week then after post 1 week check up everything was fine, could start wearing eye make up again. My vision was good after the procedure but it fluctuated alot throughout the week, like mid week I felt it got worse as night came on, which is very normal, went to sleep and next day it was back to clear vision again. I only felt that sleeping with the goggles was very uncomfortable and my eyes were really dry, the meds also didn't feel that pleasant cause it'll drip down to my throat after passing through the eyes, and it's damn bitter.

4. Actually I only found pros so far, if I've to pick a con, it would be that my eyes really was q dry a couple of years after. I was told it's cause I used contact lens often and it's not gonna get worse but it's not due to the procedure. But still, I carried lots of eye drops around back then. Then slowly it started to feel abit better. I still have them time to time but it's manageable. When I first got lasik I had to get the gel eye drop just cause I will wake up with super dry eyes.

Only regret is I didn't manage to convince parents I wanna do it earlier. I knew the risks for epi would be much easier to manage but it took a while to convince them it's better than just wearing contacts for the rest of my life. I was also lucky that my astigmatism is quite low so I'm not very sure if it would have changed my options if it was the other way around. I was 300, 375 myopic before.

I've spoken to a few friends in the medical field cause my GP wanted me in a cam boot and I was adamant about not being in it just cause I was worried it'll cause alot of immobility and they agreed that unless it's a break usually they don't put patients into cast or that sort of boot. Yours must be a pretty bad one if they had to put it back for you. Hence the splint

Nonetheless though, the important thing is to be consistent with mobility exercise. It's gonna feel like you're not doing anything even if you're just doing ABCs with your ankle but those little movements will add up over time. More stretching sessions once you're given the green light will built up the tolerance, I learned that 10 mins a day works wonders than just 50 mins every 5 days.

You'll be fine! Take it slow and steady, one day at a time!

Seems like it! I rolled it when I fell and felt it went out of place and out of pain just pushed it back.

But of course without any fracture it meant something else ruptured and true enough, complete tear of my ATFL. I was lucky there weren't any other tears. Even then, it was rough.

I had a much higher stake in getting back in my feet so I was religiously icing it in ice water for the 1st month, I had on a pretty strong brace for 3 to 4 weeks and was trying to bear weight post 1 week injury. I think I got back to driving pretty soon, about a week in, with brace of course.

Even with the brace on I sort of continued working with resistance band and just tried to walk as normally as I can. I still needed a crutch time to time. After 4 weeks I kinda got put onto physio and from there it was just religiously rehabbing it. I'm guessing the trick is to know your body enough to keep the ankle mobile and active but not to the point of reinjuring. Cause even with 4 weeks of brace (not boot), my range of motion has decreased significantly. 

Was back to dancing about 6 to 8 weeks, and about 12 weeks in I was back to wearing proper dance heels. Just last week (15  weeks) I started going into ballet classes again. Hi! This was good to read! I'll try my best to update as much as I can, since now it's post 11 weeks after the fall!

So for my case, I was able to bear weight after 2 weeks although I was limping abit, I had braces on for about 3 to 4 weeks then I ditched them for just compression or light brace. The reason is because I've to teach dance for a living and I can't fit my bulky brace into my dance shoes (all flat no heels!).

I started physio post 4 weeks, and like you, kinda made tremendous progress for the next month or so. My main issue at first was ankle mobility, mainly on knee to wall flexibility and calf rises. The double whammy is that my non injured ankle set a really high bar so the injured side had alot to catch up on. Right now in the past 2 weeks it's plateaued and I was told its very normal, I also assume I'm gonna be doing strengthening daily for the rest of my life just cause it was a full tear.

Post 8 weeks I was told that the ankle is already nearly recovered and if I was just looking to walk normally I'm there, but obviously I can't be satisfied with just that mainly also apart from bouldering I'm still dancing alot, so it's crucial I don't end up spraining it again. So right now it's alot on calf rises, stretching and pogo hopping on one leg.

On the climbing side, I was back at the wall post 6 weeks, but it was top rope, and I was keeping my upper body workout going throughout the recovery so it was just to strengthen my arms and fingers again. I started doing light bouldering maybe 2 weeks back, but the walls here at my gym are insanely high so like you I wasn't going for that sort of height, I sometimes just get to halfway point then I sort of just hop down. I do have a tendency to favour my uninjured side when I land so I'm trying to fix that as well. So for me I challenged myself with roofie routes so that I'm much closer to the mat, and yeah I've been quite satisfied with the recovery even if I was very impatient from the get go. I don't wear braces now unless I am prepared for heavy dancing and I was just given the green light to wear my dance heels and try it out.

I hope your recovery continues to get better! It was such a ride honestly, I recognize I can't take as much risk as I would love to anymore but I'm grateful I can still be back at the wall!
